Name: The Forgotten Password
Description: Your first day at the IT Helpdesk! A customer named Nika cannot sign in to his email. Talk to him and guide him to a solution. Pick an answer with the Arrow Keys and confirm with Enter. A good IT helper listens first, stays calm and never panics!

Dialogue.Npc: Hello?! Finally, a human! My email won't let me sign in. It says my password is wrong. Am I hacked?! Please tell me I'm not hacked!

Options.Text: Yes, you are 100% hacked. Unplug your computer immediately.
Options.Reply: WHAT?! Unplug it?! It's a laptop, it doesn't even have a cable! Please help me properly!

Options.Text: Let's not panic. First, check if Caps Lock is turned on.
Options.Reply: Caps Lock... OH! It was on! Good catch. But... it still says wrong password. What now?

Options.Text: Just make a new email account, it's faster.
Options.Reply: All my work contacts are in that email! I can't just abandon it. Give me real advice please!

Dialogue.Npc: So Caps Lock was on, but the password still fails. I already tried it three times!

Options.Text: No problem. Use the 'Forgot password' button and reset it via your phone or recovery email.
Options.Reply: Forgot password... found it! Okay, I got a reset message. Should I open it?

Options.Text: Type it ten more times, but faster. Sometimes that helps.
Options.Reply: ...I tried. It really, really does not help. Do you actually know what you are doing?

Options.Text: Are your fingers even on the right keys?
Options.Reply: Very funny. I came here for help, not for comedy. Let's try this seriously.

Dialogue.Npc: The reset page is open and it asks me to pick a new password. Any advice?

Options.Text: Use 'password123', it's easy to remember.
Options.Reply: My nephew says that is literally the first thing hackers try. Give me real advice!

Options.Text: Write it on a sticky note and put it on your monitor so you never forget.
Options.Reply: My whole office walks past my monitor every day... that sounds like a terrible idea!

Options.Text: Pick a long passphrase only you know, and never share it with anyone.
Options.Reply: Done! Something long and memorable... IT WORKED! I'm in! Thank you, you saved my whole week!

Name: The Missing Semicolon
Description: A junior developer left a syntax error in the helpdesk program and now it refuses to compile. Read the C# code carefully, move the cursor onto the line with the mistake and press Enter to flag it. Tip: the C# compiler is very picky about punctuation!
Fix: Every C# statement must end with a semicolon. The line should be: string welcome = "Welcome to the helpdesk";

Name: Cable Chaos
Description: Welcome to the server room! Some network cables are broken and show up as red #. Move with the Arrow Keys and press F while standing on a broken cable to fix it. Fix every cable to complete the level. Watch out for the server racks (X), you cannot walk through them!

Name: The Wrong Comparison
Description: The login program compiles, but it behaves strangely... A developer used the wrong operator somewhere in the code. Find the line with the logic mistake and press Enter to flag it. Tip: = puts a value into a variable, == checks if two values are equal!
Fix: = assigns a value, == compares two values. The line should be: if (enteredCode == correctCode)

Name: The Phishing Email
Description: Anna from accounting received a suspicious email and is about to click a dangerous link. Answer her questions and guide her to safety. Remember the golden rules of phishing: check the real sender address, never share your password, and never click links in strange emails!

Dialogue.Npc: Hi! I got an email saying my account will be closed in 24 hours unless I verify my password. Should I click the link? I don't want to lose my account!

Options.Text: Don't click anything yet. First, let's check who the email is really from.
Options.Reply: Good idea... the sender is support@totally-safe-mail-bonus.biz. Wait, that is not our company's address, is it?

Options.Text: Yes, click it quickly before your account gets closed!
Options.Reply: Hold on, it's asking for my password AND my card number. Why would IT support need my card?!

Options.Text: Just delete your whole email account to be safe.
Options.Reply: I can't delete my account, all of my invoices are in there! There has to be a better way.

Dialogue.Npc: You're right, the address looks fishy. But the email has our company logo and everything! It looks so official!

Options.Text: If it has the company logo, it must be real.
Options.Reply: Hmm, my nephew got fake 'bank' emails with perfect logos too and they were all scams...

Options.Text: Click the link, but only a little bit.
Options.Reply: That is the worst advice I have ever heard. Please take this seriously!

Options.Text: Logos are easy to copy. Always check the sender address and where the link really goes.
Options.Reply: I never thought about that. Okay, so how do I check where the link actually points?

Dialogue.Npc: Okay, I'm convinced it's fake. So what do I do with this email? And what if they keep sending more?

Options.Text: Report it as phishing, delete it, and never share your password with anyone.
Options.Reply: Reported and deleted! And from now on I'll call IT directly whenever I'm unsure. Thank you so much!

Options.Text: Reply to the scammers and tell them to stop bothering you.
Options.Reply: They wrote back saying I 'won a free iPhone'! These people are shameless!

Options.Text: Forward it to all your colleagues so they can click it too.
Options.Reply: Why would I want my colleagues to click a dangerous link?! Think before you speak!

Name: Firewall Maintenance
Description: The server hall is overheating! Five firewall nodes (red #) are failing across the network. Navigate between the server racks, stand on each failing node and press F to fix it. The racks (X) block your path, so plan your route through the aisles carefully!

Name: The Out Of Bounds Bug
Description: A senior developer left a sneaky bug behind. The program compiles fine, but at runtime it crashes with IndexOutOfRangeException! Find the line that causes the crash and press Enter to flag it. Tip: arrays start counting at 0, so the last valid index is Length - 1.
Fix: The loop runs one step too far. Use i < scores.Length instead of i <= scores.Length to stay inside the array.

Name: The Angry Client
Description: The final challenge! Giga, an angry client, storms into your office. His internet has been down for two hours and he is NOT happy. Stay professional: listen carefully, stay calm, troubleshoot step by step and never argue with the client. Good luck, you've got this!

Dialogue.Npc: TWO HOURS! My internet has been dead for TWO HOURS! I have a presentation in twenty minutes! Fix it. NOW.

Options.Text: Calm down, it's probably your own fault anyway.
Options.Reply: MY fault?! I am this close to asking for your manager! Try that again and see what happens!

Options.Text: Two hours is nothing. My internet was off for a week once.
Options.Reply: I don't care about YOUR internet! I care about MY presentation! Focus!

Options.Text: I'm really sorry about this. Let's fix it together right now. What do the lights on your router look like?
Options.Reply: ...Fine. There are lights on it. The internet one is red, I think. Is that bad? It's never red.

Dialogue.Npc: The internet light is red. What does that even mean?

Options.Text: It means your router is angry. Try apologizing to it.
Options.Reply: Are you making fun of me?! I came here for help, not for jokes!

Options.Text: A red light usually means the router lost its connection. Let's restart it and check the cable.
Options.Reply: Restart... okay, I pulled the plug and pushed the network cable back in. Do I just turn it on again?

Options.Text: Red is the new green. It means everything is fine.
Options.Reply: If everything is fine, why can't I open ONE single slide?! Help me for real!

Dialogue.Npc: Router restarted, cable pushed back in... the light is green now! Testing... IT WORKS! But wait, it's loading slowly. The presentation might still lag!

Options.Text: The router needs a minute to fully reconnect. If it's still slow I'll check your line and follow up right after your presentation.
Options.Reply: ...Alright. Alright! It's loading faster now. You were actually useful. Thank you. I take back what I said about your manager.

Options.Text: That's a router problem, not my problem. Good luck!
Options.Reply: Unbelievable! And they call THIS an IT department! Where is your supervisor?!

Options.Text: Just do the presentation without slides, like in the old days.
Options.Reply: The slides ARE the presentation! Do you even listen to people?!
